evidence.note: Foundations-first ordering: environment recon + spec search, then Python/dep install, then vendored libs curled and directories created before app code — a defensible dependency-aware sequence (storage/libs before features).
De facto done-checks tied to phases: sha256 of vendored libs immediately after download, health check after first boot — verification hooks exist in action even without stated criteria.

After each patch/restart cycle the agent verifies a spread of subsystems (statuses, timelines, profiles, admin audit, errors, webfinger, preferences, markers, static assets), showing rough subsystem breakdown — but no explicit milestone list or done-criteria are articulated.

Durability deliberately exercised (wipe DB, restart, verify persistence, re-check hashes) as a late storage-integrity check; however whole subsystems like lists, notifications/SSE, polls, and admin queues/reports show no verification, indicating the decomposition never mapped the full surface.

reasoning: The trajectory (action-only, no planning prose) reveals a sensible, dependency-aware build order — foundations (deps, vendored libs+hash) before app, then iterative per-subsystem verification, then durability — matching anchor 5's 'sensible ordered plan covering major subsystems with rough done-criteria and a defensible build order.' It falls short of 8 because there is no articulated milestone hierarchy with explicit verification hooks, no visible plan revision as scope emerged, and several major subsystems (lists, notifications/SSE, polls, admin) are never mapped or checked, so the surface was not fully covered.
